title: Election night surprise on financial sector stocks

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Classic short-horizon event study.  
Why: We want the causal effect of an unexpected election result on stock returns over an extremely short window ([+1,+3]). In liquid equity markets and narrow windows, the market-model event study is the standard quasi-experimental approach; it controls for normal co-movement with the market while isolating the shock.  

Key assumptions  
• Efficient-market/rapid-adjustment: All election-related information is incorporated immediately after the announcement, so abnormal returns in [+1,+3] are attributable to the shock.  
• No confounding firm-specific news in the three-day window.  
• Stable market model: Parameters (αᵢ,βᵢ) estimated on the clean pre-event window [−10,−2] remain valid during [+1,+3].  
• Cross-sectional independence (or weak dependence) so that the t-tests on the average CAR are valid asymptotically.  

## 2. R Code
```r
# ================================================================
# Election-night event study on financial sector stocks
# ================================================================
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(broom)

# 1. ----------------------------------------------------------------
# Read data
file_path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s15_data.csv"
dat <- read_csv(file_path, col_types = cols())

# 2. ----------------------------------------------------------------
# Define windows
est_win   <- -10:-2          # estimation window
event_win <-  1:3            # main event window (+1 to +3)
alt_win   <-  0:3            # robustness window (0 to +3)

# 3. ----------------------------------------------------------------
# Estimate market-model parameters α_i and β_i on [−10,−2]
params <- dat %>%
  filter(event_day %in% est_win) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  do({
    fit <- lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = .)
    tibble(alpha = coef(fit)[1],
           beta  = coef(fit)[2])
  })

# 4. ----------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: function to compute abnormal returns & CARs
get_CAR <- function(window_vec, param_tbl, name){
  dat %>%
    filter(event_day %in% window_vec) %>%
    left_join(param_tbl, by = "stock_id") %>%
    mutate(ab_ret = ret - (alpha + beta * mkt_ret)) %>%
    group_by(stock_id) %>%
    summarise(CAR = sum(ab_ret), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(window = name)
}

car_main <- get_CAR(event_win, params, "1_3")
car_alt  <- get_CAR(alt_win  , params, "0_3")

# 5. ----------------------------------------------------------------
# Cross-sectional t-tests
tt_main <- t.test(car_main$CAR)
tt_alt  <- t.test(car_alt$CAR)

# 6. ----------------------------------------------------------------
# ROBUSTNESS 1: Use supplied β (constant) instead of re-estimated β
car_givenbeta <- dat %>%
  filter(event_day %in% event_win) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  mutate(alpha = mean(ret - beta * mkt_ret)) %>%   # constant mean adjustment
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(ab_ret = ret - (alpha + beta * mkt_ret)) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR = sum(ab_ret), .groups = "drop")

tt_givenbeta <- t.test(car_givenbeta$CAR)

# 7. ----------------------------------------------------------------
# Print concise numerical results
cat("===============================================================\n")
cat("Election-night surprise: Financial stocks, [+1,+3] window\n")
cat("---------------------------------------------------------------\n")
cat(sprintf("Average CAR (+1,+3): %6.4f\n", mean(car_main$CAR)))
cat(sprintf("t-statistic: %6.3f ,  p-value: %6.4f\n",
            tt_main$statistic, tt_main$p.value))
cat("---------------------------------------------------------------\n")
cat("Robustness checks\n")
cat(sprintf("Alt window (+0,+3):  CAR = %6.4f ,  p = %6.4f\n",
            mean(car_alt$CAR),  tt_alt$p.value))
cat(sprintf("Given β (+1,+3):     CAR = %6.4f ,  p = %6.4f\n",
            mean(car_givenbeta$CAR), tt_givenbeta$p.value))
cat("===============================================================\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Positive.  
Rationale: In historical U.S. episodes, an unexpectedly pro-business, deregulatory electoral outcome (e.g., 2016) boosted bank/financial stocks because of expected rollback of regulation and lower taxes. The surprise component should therefore create positive abnormal returns.  

Magnitude: For a three-day window we expect roughly +1½ % abnormal return on average across the 80 financial stocks, i.e., CAR ≈ +0.015 with a cross-sectional t-stat around 3, leading to p-values below 1 %.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study — political event; market model; focus on [+1,+3] for after-hours announcement
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Financial stocks earned positive abnormal returns after election surprise
